1.note: The expression **were born** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [whom his wives bore to him]

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **second**, you could represent this number, as well the similar numbers in the next two verses and in verse 15, in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [son number two, Daniel]

4.note: See how you translated the expression “were born” in [3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [His wives bore him these six sons]

5.note: The traditional Hebrew text reads “Bathshua.” The ULT follows that reading. One ancient manuscript and one ancient version read “Bathsheba” here, which is the form of this woman’s name in chapters 11 and 12 of 2 Samuel and chapters 1 and 2 of 1 Kings. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

9.note: The author assumes that readers will understand that he means that he has listed **All of the sons** of David’s full legal wives. Those were the sons who had inheritance rights, including the right potentially to become king. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [These are all of the sons whom David had by his full legal wives]

21.note: The author uses the singular term **son** even though he then names two sons of Hananiah. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a plural term here and in similar instances in the book. Alternate translation: [And the sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah]

22.note: The number **six** appears in the traditional Hebrew text. Since only five names are listed, many interpreters believe that a name dropped out during the process of copying. You may want to follow an alternative reading from two ancient versions. Alternate translation: [Hattush and Igal and Bariah and Neariah and Azariah and Shaphat]
